title: EU Adopts First-Ever Science Diplomacy Framework; Horizon Europe 2028-34 Debated
detail: The EU Competitiveness Council (Research and Space configuration) met on May 29 and adopted a Council Recommendation establishing the EU's first-ever formal Science Diplomacy framework. The recommendation defines how the EU will use scientific cooperation as a foreign policy instrument — strengthening international research partnerships, projecting the EU's soft power through research excellence, and supporting global access to knowledge. Ministers also held an orientation debate on Horizon Europe 2028-2034, the Commission's proposed €175 billion successor to the current framework programme (submitted July 2025). Ministers gave guidance on scope, participation models for non-EU countries, synergies with the Defence Fund, and the programme's mission-driven architecture. The Council was also briefed on the proposed EU Space Act, a comprehensive harmonised framework for EU space activities covering safety, resilience, environmental sustainability, and European space industry competitiveness in a rapidly commercialising sector.

title: Revised EU Buildings Directive (EPBD) Transposition Deadline: Zero-Emission Standards Enter National Law
detail: May 29, 2026 was the mandatory transposition deadline for EU member states to incorporate the revised Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD, Directive EU/2024/1275) into national law. The revised EPBD — adopted in 2024 — requires all new buildings to be zero-emission by 2030, mandates renovation of the 16% worst-performing non-residential buildings by 2030, and sets a target to reduce average residential building energy use by at least 16% by 2030 versus 2020 levels. The directive also strengthens minimum energy performance standards for commercial buildings and requires solar panels on all new public and commercial buildings by 2027. The old Directive 2010/31/EU is formally repealed as of May 30. Buildings account for approximately 40% of the EU's total energy consumption and 36% of CO2 emissions, making the EPBD a central pillar of the EU Green Deal's Renovation Wave.
